length.statement: The shortest article has 101 words, above the 50-word level below which a text is a snippet rather than an article, so no minimum length is applied. 398 of 3146 documents are under 250 words; the model results by length bucket are checked in the first evaluation run (results/tables).

baseline_all_docs.top_coefficient_note: No website-name token among the top 25 words per class.

removal_rate_difference_test.test: Fisher exact on documents (ignores that documents of one website are alike)

comparison_with_all_docs.note: The validation sets differ (all validation documents vs only the on-topic ones), so the F1 values of rows A and C are NOT directly comparable. Row B scores the all-documents model on exactly the documents of row C. Differences are descriptive; no significance test is claimed.

rows.setting: A: all-docs model, all validation docs (first run)
B: all-docs model, filtered validation docs (like-for-like)
C: filtered model, filtered validation docs

ablation.data: filtered documents, split_v1, validation rows only
ablation.protocol: per model: C in C_GRID x class_weight in (none, balanced), best conspiracy-F1 on validation

chosen_lr.rule: M2 only if delta-F1 vs M1 has a website-bootstrap CI above 0 on validation

llm.selection_rule: chosen prompt = highest conspiracy-F1 on filtered VALIDATION documents (rounded to 4 digits); tie -> fewer input tokens (cheaper). Fixed and written to metrics.json before any test document is classified.
llm.question: source: conspiracy-oriented or mainstream website

test.pass_scored: pass 1 (official; pass 2 is a sensitivity check)

comparison.data: filtered documents, split_v1, TEST rows; predictions from evaluate_final files only

errors.data: TEST rows, filtered documents; predictions from evaluate_final files only
errors.rule: conspiracy site + (rejects|neutral|no_claim) -> label problem; mainstream site + endorses -> label problem; else model wrong
